newsitem.title: USA: Late NYMEX Hub natgas holds modest gains with cash.
newsitem.headline: Late NYMEX Hub natgas holds modest gains with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures held modest gains late Wednesday in fairly active trade, still underpinned by reports of firmer physical prices despite mostly mild Midwest and Northeast weather this week.
At 1350 EDT, August was still up 2.7 cents at $2.144 per million British thermal units, while September was 1.7 cents higher at $2.09. Most others were up by one-half to 1.7 cents.

"There are no hurricanes left and the weather is nothing to get excited about. We're still stuck in a range," said one Houston-based trader, noting cash firmed slightly again today and seemed well-supported at these levels.
Forecasters expect Midwest and Northeast temperatures to warm to a few degrees F above-normal by the weekend, then cool to more seasonal levels next week.

Chart traders agreed August was range bound, with support at $2.07 and then at the $2.051 low from July 8. Major trendline resistance this week was seen in the low-$2.20s, with further resistance pegged at the $2.29 and $2.36 prominent highs. Most said it would take an August close above the trendline to turn sentiment decidedly bullish.
A Reuter poll of industry players showed most expected a weekly AGA stock build in the 75-80 bcf range when the report is released later today. Last year, stocks gained 90 bcf.
In the cash Wednesday, Gulf Coast prices firmed three cents to the mid-to-high teens. Midcon pipes were four cents higher at about $2.10. New York city gate gas was up slightly at about $2.40.
NYMEX said 29,684 contracts traded at 1315 EDT.
On the KCBT, August climbed 3.4 cents to $2.07, while deferreds were steady to one-half cent higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.7 cent to 7.4 cents (NYMEX premium).
